text:
Recent work supports checking individual claims against evidence rather than trusting semantic similarity. [Kabongo and Guigue (2025/2026)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2512.24366) find strong BERTScore alongside poor statement-level factual precision in recommendation explanations. Their review-derived supervision is unavailable here, but the diagnostic principle transfers: extract atomic claims and attach supporting title/description spans. Proposed adaptation: label compatibility claims as supported, explicitly contradicted, or unknown; distinguish broad topical relatedness from evidence of required interfaces, models, dimensions, or prerequisites. Missing specifications justify uncertainty, not an incompatibility finding.

Interaction history also needs cautious interpretation. [Li et al. (2025)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2502.09869), interviewing 34 social-media users, distinguish consumption from intentional feedback used to reshape recommendations. [Learning to Forget (2026)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.12714) models purchases as potentially terminating demand, while allowing replenishment cycles. Its purchase-specific assumptions cannot establish ownership or satiation from this task’s generic interactions. Therefore, flag near-duplicate titles/descriptions as potential redundancy; reserve claims of fulfilled demand or intent mismatch for explicit evidence. Validate diagnostic labels against available qualitative feedback, distinguishing real user statements from simulator judgments.

For uncertain judgments, [ReCoVERR (2024)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2402.15610) offers a transferable pattern: seek additional evidence before abstaining, reducing unnecessary abstention in visual reasoning. Applied here, inspect available descriptions for decisive specifications, then abstain on unsupported diagnostic claims. Evaluate diagnostic error versus coverage on annotated examples. This is an extrapolation from another domain, not demonstrated recommendation performance; diagnostic abstention should preserve the benchmark’s required rankings and macro validation HR@10 selection.
